newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks trend down on US bond weakness.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks trend down on US bond weakness.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks dropped sharply in early morning trading in response to weakness in the U.S. long bond market and ahead of the U.S. August jobs report due later on Friday, analysts said.
The Hang Seng was down 100 points at 10,940. Turnover was HK$479 million after the first twenty-five minutes of trading.
"We expect to see some weakness this morning but not a lot of volume, said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia."
Lesko said he did not expect to see aggressive selling in Hong Kong in advance of the jobs report and the bond market's reaction to that data.
Chris Sawtell, director of technical strategy at W.I.Carr, said the Hang Seng Index will be unlikely to hold at 11,000.
"But (U.S.) bonds are deeply oversold and if the U.S. unemployment report is favourable, we could get a reversal in bonds next week," Sawtell said.
The Hang Seng Index has followed the trend in the U.S.long bond market for years, according to Sawtell.
Hong Kong's response to movements in that market, however, is often more modest than the original move, he added.

Traders said Hong Kong investors were unlikely to trade aggressively in advance of the weekend and economic data reports that could suggest a coming rise in U.S. and local interest rates and subsequent fall in bond markets.
Big cap stocks with heavy weights in the Hang Seng Index saw the greatest declines in early Friday trading.
Swire Pacific A was hit by profit-taking which wiped out HK$0.75 to bring the share to HK$67.00 in early trading.
Prices of interest rate sensitive issues, particularly banks, were shaved. HSBC Holdings fell HK$1.00 to HK$131.00, as did Hang Seng Bank to HK$77.25.
Trading in shares of Universal Appliances were suspended at the company's request pending an announcement. The share rose HK$0.001 to HK$0.201 on Thursday.

Pacific Concord was active. The share shed HK$0.10 to HK$1.89 following a statement by the company that it planned to spin off its Hong Kong and China properties in a separate listing. No details on the cost of property transfers from Pacific Concord to the new entity were given or a timetable for the spinoff.
